title: Students strike demanding a national university
why: Student mobilisation led to the creation of the Lebanese University later that year.

title: Council of Ministers meets after student university campaign
why: Cabinet responded to the January strike; the Lebanese University was formally established on 3 December 1951.

title: Chamoun, Gemayel, Eddé, Jumblatt ally against Khoury
why: Cross-sectarian opposition front that prepared the 1952 campaign forcing President Khoury to resign.

title: Patriotic Socialist Front adopts left-leaning programme
why: Opposition front around Chamoun and Jumblatt set out reform demands months before Khoury resigned.

title: Opposition front holds rally in Chamoun's hometown
why: Part of the mounting campaign that preceded the September 1952 general strike and Khoury resignation.

title: Fouad Chehab serves as acting president for four days
why: Army commander and prime minister bridged the gap after Khoury resigned, until 22 September 1952.

title: Chamoun signs trade agreement with Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Syria
why: Early Arab trade opening under Chamoun after the 1950 customs split with Syria.

title: Trans Mediterranean Airways starts as non-scheduled carrier
why: Beirut-based cargo airline that became a regional freight player; scheduled all-cargo status followed in 1959.

title: Chamoun government receives $6 million in US arms and aid
why: US economic and military aid grew under Chamoun alongside closer Western alignment.

title: World Bank approves $27 million loan for Litani project
why: Foreign-exchange financing for the Litani hydropower and irrigation scheme; parliament ratified later.

title: BOAC takes 49 percent of Middle East Airlines
why: Foreign shareholding replaced Pan Am; BOAC association ended 16 August 1961.

title: Middle East Airlines introduces Vickers Viscount
why: First turboprop airliners on MEA routes, ahead of the Comet jets of 1960.

title: Litani authority announces Zouk Mikael thermal plant
why: Plan to add generating capacity near Beirut and back up Litani hydro; shows early power shortages.

title: Cornerstone laid for Télé Liban television station
why: Chamoun era groundwork for television; CLT began broadcasting 28 May 1959.

title: Chamoun founds National Liberal Party
why: Post-presidency party that later led the Tripartite Alliance and the Christian right.

title: US forces complete withdrawal from Lebanon
why: Operation Blue Bat peaked at more than 14,000 US personnel, 8,509 Army and 5,670 Marines.

title: Decree creates Council on Money and Credit
why: First step toward a national central bank; activation was delayed under opposition including the president.

title: Decree 150 puts autonomous agencies under ministry trusteeship
why: Chehab-era control of public agencies such as the Litani authority; ministry official on every board.

title: Chehab presents resignation, then stays in office
why: Chehab tendered his resignation on 20 July 1960 two years into his term and was persuaded to remain.

title: Markabi hydropower plant enters service on the Litani
why: First Litani scheme plant operating by January 1962; an IBRD staffer judged its appearance harshly.

title: Military tribunal indicts Intra founder Beidas
why: Press campaign alleged trading with Israel and corruption; Beidas and allies disputed these claims; fed Intra rivalries.

title: Cedar-3 rocket launched
why: Heavy Lebanese Rocket Society rocket, 6.80 m long, launched during the Chehab-funded programme.

title: Middle East Airlines merges with Air Liban
why: Merger gave Air France 30 percent of the enlarged MEA.
dup_of: Middle East Airlines merges with Air Liban

title: Musa al-Sadr opens Girls Home and Institute of Islamic Studies in Tyre
why: Early Shia social institutions built before his political movement.

title: Musa al-Sadr starts Burj al-Shimali technical institute
why: Vocational school funded by benefactors, bank loans and the education ministry.

title: Former president Bechara el-Khoury dies in Beirut
why: First president of independent Lebanon died aged 73, 12 years after his 1952 resignation.

title: Chehab refuses constitutional amendment for a second term
why: Refusal enabled Charles Helou election in August 1964 and shaped the Chehabist succession.

title: Middle East Airlines adopts its current name
why: Name settled after the 1963 Air Liban merger.

title: Court appoints auditors, including Price Waterhouse, over Intra Bank
why: Judge Ghandour ordered an outside audit weeks after Intra stopped payments; Cooper Brothers later replaced Price Waterhouse.

title: Court declares Intra Bank bankrupt on a provisional basis
why: Judge Ghandour rejected a concordat petition; ruling was widely reported and contested by Intra insiders.

title: Colour television broadcasts begin on SECAM
why: Very early in the region; reached only ten sets at launch.
dup_of: CLT among first in world to broadcast in colour (SECAM)

title: General amnesty releases jailed SSNP activists
why: Amnesty ended years of imprisonment or exile after the 1961 coup attempt; party moved toward Arab nationalism.

title: Popular Front attacks Trans-Arabian Pipeline
why: PFLP attack on the Golan section, held by Israel since 1967, hit the line that ended at Sidon.

title: Musa al-Sadr becomes first head of Supreme Islamic Shia Council
why: Created a state-recognised Shia body, a step in the community's institutional rise.

title: Unofficial text of Cairo Agreement printed in An-Nahar
why: The official text was never published; only this unofficial version circulated.

title: Suleiman Frangieh sworn in as president
why: Won by one vote (50-49) after Jumblatt supporters switched; term ran to 22 September 1976.

title: 16,000 public school teachers strike
why: Teachers and tobacco farmers struck in January 1973, showing public-sector and rural unrest before the war.

title: Funeral of three PLO leaders draws about 250,000
why: Funeral after Israel's raid; about 10 percent of the population attended; Salam cabinet resigned.

title: Musa al-Sadr and Husseini co-found Movement of the Disinherited
why: Wikipedia dates the movement to 6 July 1974; an earlier Baalbek rally is dated 17 March.

title: Foreign exchange controls eliminated entirely
why: Lebanon moved to a fully free exchange regime, a base of its financial hub model; controls had been eased from 1948.

title: An-Nahar publishes parliamentary report on Telephones Authority scandal
why: Staff of the authority had grown from 380 to 2,200 between 1947 and 1951; cited as patronage example.

title: Automatic telephone dialling introduced
why: Network modernised with about 27,000 telephones in Lebanon at the time.

title: Litani authority announces then reverses contract award to Parsons and Harza
why: Cost miscalculation by the US group forced a reversal; delays marked the early Litani project.

title: Zouk thermal power station begins operating
why: Added generating capacity near Beirut under the state Electricity Office created in 1954.

title: Statistical institute created and Civil Service Council set up
why: Part of Chehab's administrative reform by decree-law after the 1958 crisis.

title: Legislative Decree 112 creates the Civil Service Board
why: Merit-based recruitment board covering most ministries and autonomous agencies except army, security and judiciary; date given as 12/6/1959.

title: Chehab commissions IRFED study of Lebanon's regions
why: French institute led by Father Lebret studied cities and 80 rural areas, the base of Chehabist development policy.

title: Henry Naccache becomes Litani authority president
why: Naccache and director Salah Halwani revived the stalled project; the dam later bore his father's name.

title: Jumblatt founds National Struggle Front, wins 11 seats
why: Jumblatt's front entered parliament in the 1960 elections.

title: IRFED finds about half of households poor or destitute
why: Study showed Beirut-periphery inequality; many poor neighbourhoods had incomes under LL 2,500 a year.

title: IRFED findings submitted to government with 140+ indicators
why: Report became the reference for Chehab-era reform and later critiques of the golden age.

title: Lebanon introduces telex service
why: Telex service began in 1962, which the source calls a first in the Arab world.

title: Philippe Takla appointed first Banque du Liban governor
why: Served until 6 June 1967; the bank started operating on 1 April 1964 under Decree 13513.

title: Communist Party joins Front for Progressive Parties and National Forces
why: End of the party's isolation; the front later evolved into the Lebanese National Movement.

title: Lebanon suspends Hasbani river diversion after Israeli warnings
why: Arab League diversion works of 1965 were hit by Israeli attacks (March, May, August 1965 on Syrian sites).

title: Work starts on Joun power plant; Naccache resignation accepted
why: Fifth resignation of Litani chief Henry Naccache accepted in 1967 after political and administrative resistance.

title: First satellite earth station opens at Arbaniyeh
why: Lebanon joined the Intelsat network.

title: First submarine coaxial cable to Marseille opens; Sodetel founded
why: Sodetel was set up to run the new international link.

title: Jumblatt, as interior minister, legalises Communist Party
why: Party banned since 1948; legalisation allowed leaders to run in 1972 elections without winning seats.

title: Chehab says he cannot run again without constitutional change
why: Declaration reopened the field and led to the one-vote election of Frangieh.

title: Decree 1943 to raise customs duties on 500+ goods; merchants strike
why: Ten-day merchant strike killed the decree, showing the power of the commercial elite.

title: Health Minister Emile Bitar resigns in protest
why: Resigned from the cabinet over what the source portrays as the government's policy failures.

title: About one million visitors enter Lebanon in one year
why: US State Department figures: 619,000 Arabs and 310,000 Westerners; Syrian workers excluded.

title: Jumblatt elected Secretary General of the Arab Front
why: Front backed the Palestinian cause; a step toward the left-Palestinian alliance of 1975.

title: UN creates Economic Commission for Western Asia
why: Successor to the UN office in Beirut; the secretariat sat in Beirut from 1974 and returned in 1997.

title: Lebanon grants citizenship to about 50,000 Christian Palestinian refugees
why: Naturalisation of mostly Christian refugees during the 1950s and 1960s, unlike other refugees.

title: Chamoun refuses to cut ties with Britain and France over Suez
why: Refusal angered Nasser and Muslim leaders and fed the opposition behind the 1958 crisis.

title: Saeb Salam and Abdallah Yafi resign over Suez stance
why: Prime minister and oil minister quit in protest at Chamoun policy toward the Suez attackers; date from a search summary.

title: Chehab and Nasser meet in a tent on the Lebanese-Syrian border
why: Summit reassured Nasser on Lebanese territory and settled Lebanon's sovereignty after 1958 crisis.

title: Office of Planning and Social Development set up under Chehab
why: One of several Chehabist bodies created in 1958-64, with planning and tourism councils and a public housing institute.

title: First National Plan of Development formally adopted
why: IRFED-based plan of 1961-62 steered public works to the periphery; Chehab-era planning peak.

title: Decree 13955 creates National Social Security Fund
why: Autonomous fund with a board of 10 employer, 10 worker and 6 state members; benefits rolled out in stages.
dup_of: National Social Security Fund created by Chehab decree

title: First Arab League summit opens in Cairo
why: Lebanon attended; leaders backed a plan to divert the Hasbani and Banias and a unified Arab command.

title: Palestine Liberation Organization is formed
why: Created after the January Arab summit; PLO armed presence later became central in Lebanon.

title: Israel attacks Arab diversion works in March, May and August
why: Strikes ended the Arab plan to divert the Jordan headwaters; Lebanon suspended its Hasbani work in July.

title: First Hawker Hunter jets arrive for the Lebanese Air Force
why: Air force founded in 1949 reached jet fighters; Mirage IIIEL jets followed in 1968.

title: Two Lebanese Hawker Hunters strafe Galilee; one shot down
why: Lebanon's only combat role in the Six-Day War; an Israeli Mirage downed one jet.

title: France delivers 12 Mirage IIIEL fighters to Lebanon
why: Delivered months before the Israeli raid on Beirut airport; funds later limited use of the fleet.

title: Legislative Decree 11614 regulates foreign property purchases
why: Required Council of Ministers approval for non-Arab buyers; amended by Law 296/2001.

title: Council for the South set up by legislative decree
why: Public body created to compensate southerners for Israeli attack damage and fund development in the south.

title: Green Plan created by Decree 13335
why: Autonomous authority under the agriculture minister for land reclamation, hill lakes and rural roads.

title: NSSF sickness and maternity branch starts operating
why: First major branch began seven years after the 1963 decree; date from a search summary.

title: Press alleges irregular gold dealings at Banque de Syrie et du Liban
why: The finance minister admitted bypassing IMF gold-trading rules; episode fed pressure for a national central bank.
actors: Banque de Syrie et du Liban

title: Beirut residents begin six-month boycott of electricity bills
why: Consumer strike against Electricité de Beyrouth over rates and service ended in June with a 22 percent tariff cut.

title: Government decrees 22 percent electricity rate cut to end boycott
why: Rates cut with effect from the strike start in January; paved the way to the state buying the company in March 1954.

title: Parliament approves World Bank Litani loan
why: Ratified the loan after debate over regions covered by irrigation; the first big state-led hydro project.

title: Astaldi wins contract for 16 km Awali tunnel
why: Italian firm began work on the tunnel feeding the Awali power station; progress was slow.

title: Kataeb calls general strike in Christian areas
why: Strike in east Beirut and Mount Lebanon during the post-July "counter-rebellion" over cabinet formation.

title: United Unions threaten general strike unless a government forms
why: Threat helped trigger the four-minister cabinet that ended the 1958 crisis the same day.

title: First major collapse in Litani Awali tunnel
why: Sand blocked three kilometres; further cave-ins ran to January 1960 and an inquiry blamed contractors.

title: Record number of strikes in modern Lebanese history
why: US embassy count: about two dozen major strikes, including a 28-day Beirut airport stoppage and cement plant strikes.

title: US interest-rate rise cuts Gulf capital inflows to Beirut banks
why: Dissertation traces the Intra run to higher US and European rates draining deposits from Beirut.

title: Cabinet approves plan to divert a third of Litani flow
why: Plan for 15,000 hectares in a minister's south Lebanon seat; Litani chief Salah Helwani resigned in protest.

title: Intra founder Beidas, a fugitive in Brazil, calls collapse a conspiracy
why: Interview with Life magazine; he blamed rivals including bankers' association head Pierre Eddé.

title: Government ends subsidy for Litani electricity
why: Cabinet told the Litani authority to cut tariffs, threatening its debt service.

title: Security forces clash with Palestinian fighters
why: First clash of the period between the army and the PLO factions before the December Beirut airport raid.

title: Army suppresses pro-PLO demonstrations in Beirut and Sidon
why: Scores killed or wounded according to the source; Prime Minister Karami resigned on 24 April.

title: Army campaign against Palestinian groups; Syria closes border
why: Syrian border closure and blockade forced Lebanon toward the Cairo Agreement.

title: Industrial exports rise as Lebanon's export base shifts
why: Total exports grew from about LL450 million (1967) to over LL2.1 billion (1974); manufactured share 42 to 79 percent (1965 to 1974).

title: About 84 percent of deposits held by foreign-controlled banks
why: Dissertation estimate for the early 1970s after post-Intra foreign takeovers across the banking sector.

title: Left forces form Lebanese National Movement, per one study
why: Dissertation dates the coalescence to June 1973; other histories date the front earlier or later.

title: Zahrani refinery commissioned near Sidon
why: Caltex-owned MEDRECO plant, 17,500 barrels a day; Tapline crude reached the neighbouring terminal. Operated until 1989.

title: New 30-32 inch IPC pipeline to Tripoli completed
why: Added to the 1934 and 1946 lines; crude pumping to Tripoli halted in 1972 after nationalisations in Iraq and Syria.

title: Crude pumping to Tripoli stops after Iraq and Syria nationalisations
why: Ended the Kirkuk-Tripoli flow that had run since 1934; the state took over the installations in 1973.

title: State takes over management of Tripoli and Zahrani oil installations
why: Lebanese government assumed management of both refinery terminals; Tripoli refinery was suspended in 1992.

title: AUB board announces 10 percent tuition rise
why: Rise for 1974-75 set off the March 1974 student occupation of the American University of Beirut.

title: Students occupy AUB buildings over fees
why: Occupation followed rejection of demands on 16 March; the academic year was suspended on 5 April.

title: Security forces raid AUB and arrest 61 students
why: Raid ended a 37-day occupation per this source; the administration suspended the Student Council the next day.

title: AUB bars 103 students from registration
why: Follow-up discipline after the occupation and the April raid.

title: Students protest army attacks on Palestinian fedayeen
why: Spring 1968 protests began a wave of student demonstrations over Palestine and US policy that ran to 1973.

title: General strike in Tripoli
why: Le Monde reported on 24 December 1973 that Beirut and Tripoli demonstrations had raised tension.

title: Lebanese-born population in Australia reaches 24,000
why: Emigration to Australia rose after the 1967 war; the 1976 census counted 33,000.

title: BLOM Bank starts operating in Beirut
why: Founders included politician Hussein Oweini; its first overseas branch opened in Jeddah in 1953.

title: BLOM opens first overseas branch in Jeddah
why: Early sign of Lebanese banks following Gulf oil money.

title: Second Bureau restructured with extra powers after SSNP coup attempt
why: Military intelligence became a main political actor under Chehab, accused of electoral interference.

title: Audi incorporated as a bank
why: Family house founded in 1830 became a licensed bank during the banking boom.

title: Emile Bustani buys Grand Hotel for redevelopment
why: Hotel finished by his family in 1967 as the Al Bustan Hotel, part of the tourism build-up.

title: Contractor and MP Emile Bustani dies in plane crash off Beirut
why: Founder of the regional contractor CAT; his daughter Myrna later became the first woman elected to parliament.

title: Byblos Bank formally established and opens in Jbeil
why: Registered with the new central bank; the firm dated from 1950 as a silk, leather and agricultural credit house.

title: Bank of Beirut founded as Realty Business Bank
why: Renamed Bank of Beirut in 1970; one of many banks founded during the boom.

title: Banque Libano-Francaise incorporated under Lebanese law
why: French-owned bank, present since 1930 as a branch, became a Lebanese joint-stock company.

title: BFMO buys the Lebanese branch that became Fransabank
why: Branch opened in 1921 as part of a French-Maghreb bank; named Fransabank in 1982.

title: Beirut airport raid hits Lebanese International Airways as well
why: Airport page counts 14 civilian aircraft destroyed; MEA recovered while Lebanese International Airways later failed.
dup_of: Israel destroys 13 civilian aircraft at Beirut airport

title: Supreme Islamic Shia Council founded
why: State-recognised body to give the Shia community an institutional voice; Musa al-Sadr led it as president.

title: Kataeb, National Liberal Party and National Bloc announce Tripartite Alliance
why: Christian-led bloc against Chehabism; the concept dated from a 23 March 1967 meeting.

title: National Bloc quits Tripartite Alliance over Cairo Agreement
why: Kataeb and the National Liberal Party later formed the Lebanese Front in 1976.

title: Hussein el-Husseini enters parliament aged 35
why: Future Amal leader and Speaker (1984-1992) won a seat in the last pre-war election.

title: Holiday Inn opens in Beirut
why: 26-storey, 400-room hotel built from 1971; a landmark of pre-war tourism, later fought over in the Battle of the Hotels.

title: Beirut port operator renamed Gestion et Exploitation du Port de Beyrouth
why: French concession company, held since 1887, was renamed in 1960.

title: Beirut foreign exchange market becomes the main one in the region
why: After exchange controls were eased 1948-52, Beirut became a hub; the source says the CIA used it to move covert funds.

title: Government reforms complete free trade and capital regime
why: Monetary Law, end of the Syrian customs union, exchange liberalisation 1948-52 and quota removal set the post-1950 model; industrialists protested.

title: Palestinian factions take over army barracks on the Israeli border
why: Early skirmishes cost the army casualties; the PLO later assumed control of central areas of Sidon and Tyre.

title: Maarouf Saad founds Popular Nasserite Organization
why: Sidon MP (1957-1972) built a Nasserist movement; he was shot on 26 February 1975 at a fishermen's protest.

title: Fouad Afram al-Bustani becomes Lebanese University president
why: Served until 1970 through the university's first two decades; Edmond Naim succeeded him.

title: Chehab hands over to Helou after a six-year term
why: Chehab Foundation tallies about 1,150 villages served and 380 new municipalities; minimum wage 94 to 125 LL. (handover date per Wikipedia Helou page; Chehab Foundation tallies from fouadchehab.org/presidency not re-checked)
